message:

The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: I need to verify that the refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds recorded in my system before recording any payouts. I will call list_refunds to retrieve the recorded refunds.
The refunds reported by Alpha Co match the recorded refunds exactly, so I can proceed to calculate each customer's net balance using net_balance.

The net_balance tool returned an error indicating that customer '192' does not exist. I need to determine which customers are the owners of the refunded orders (192, 193, 194) by listing the orders and identifying the corresponding customer IDs.

I have the order details. Refund order 192 belongs to customer 'cobalt', order 193 to 'acme', and order 194 to 'birch'. I need to compute each customer’s net balance (order amounts minus refunds) using net_balance, then record payouts. I'll start by getting net_balance for 'cobalt'.
I have cobalt' net balance (18779 cents). Next I need acme' net balance. I will call net_balance for customer 'acme'.
I have acme' net balance 33841 cents. Now I need birch' net balance. I will call net_balance for customer 'birch'.
I now have all customers' net balances: cobalt 18779 cents, acme 33841 cents, birch 34692 cents. I will record the payouts for each customer using record_payout.
The payout for cobalt has been recorded successfully. Next, I will record the payout for acme.

reply.thought: The previous record_ payout call failed due to a typo in the argument name ('amount_cent' instead of 'amount_cents'). I need to correct the argument name and resend the record_ payout request for acme.
The previous attempt failed because of a typo in the tool name ("record_ payout" with a space). I need to use the correct tool name "record_payout" without the space.
The payout for acme has been recorded successfully. Now I need to record the payout for birch.
All payouts have been recorded successfully. I will now finish the task by reporting the payouts.
